title: EA LAB Factory OS - entity schemas (DESIGN ONLY, rev 2 after the 2026-07-30 blind audit)
description: Appendix to _triage/EA_LAB_FACTORY_OS_DESIGN.md. REV 2 answers audit finding P0-1: rev 1 put every schema under $defs with no root type/properties/oneOf, so validating any instance against this FILE accepted almost anything and a slice could have reported 'schema-valid' while no contract ran at all. The root is now a discriminated union on `entity`, so validating against the file itself resolves to exactly one entity schema and unknown shapes are rejected. Every entity also sets unevaluatedProperties:false. Nothing here is implemented; no validator consumes it yet.

x-ea-lab-meta.blocking_gate: no taskboard Order may be written until the revised design passes re-review
validator_contract: A conforming validator MUST validate each instance against this root, which resolves via `entity` to exactly one $defs schema. Validating against $defs/<Entity> directly is also permitted; validating against the file with no entity discriminator is NOT a conformance claim.
Every entity requires negative fixtures. A schema that has never rejected anything is untested - the same rule this repo applies to guards.

Constraints stated only in prose in rev 1 (transitions, immutability, permissions, reconciliation) are NOT expressible in JSON Schema. They carry x-enforced-by, and a field carrying it is a reminder that the schema does NOT check it. CORRECTED 2026-07-31 (Codex audit 7 MAJOR 7): this used to say the named validator MUST exist, which made the field false governance state -- 7 of the 10 names had no implementation at all. x-enforcement-status now says which: PLANNED (named, not built - the constraint is enforced by NOTHING today), BUILT (x-enforcer exists and has negative fixtures, but nothing calls it in production), WIRED (BUILT and actually invoked by a hook or the pre-commit tier). Only WIRED means the constraint is enforced. check_schema_structure.py verifies each claim against the repo.
forbidden_everywhere: any MUTABLE copy of a fact owned elsewhere - store a pinned reference (path + commit_oid + blob_oid + raw_sha256) instead. Audit finding P0-2: rev 1 stored mutable copies of coverage state, work status, run occurrence and deployment identity, all of which already have owners.

contracts._why: BACKLOG-D31. Not every normative contract is a JSON entity. These are the ones that are not, held here so the design's tables can be GENERATED from them instead of retyped. Audit-3 finding #12 (the pilot parity list) is exactly this shape: it was bound to nothing machine-readable, so it drifted freely and no checker could see it.

parameter_registry_columns._why: Audit-1 finding #10 REGRESSED because `role` was described as a column of the global registry while the schema put it per-hypothesis in ParameterBinding. Locked-ness is per hypothesis: the same input can be LOCKED in B14-H01 and TUNABLE in B14-H02, and marking it globally makes optimize_guard refuse it on every Boss. This table is the reason a `role` column reappearing here is now a schema change, not a prose edit.

rows.meaning: what the CODE does with the number, not what the name claims - the chassis holds two meanings of 'pip' at once
where in the strategy it applies
the condition under which this input has any effect at all
inputs that must move with it or the strategy changes rather than resizes
the question a sweep of this input answers
OPERATOR / TUNING / OVERRIDE / DEAD - OVERRIDE means member of a precedence chain, NOT dead (Stage 0A P0)
the label the generated Inputs page shows
the enum type when the input is an enum, so a diff table cannot compare a name against a number
which sibling wins when an OVERRIDE chain has more than one member set
ABSENT FROM THIS TABLE ON PURPOSE - role/locked_value/safe_range/optimize_stage are per-hypothesis and live in factory/parameter_bindings.jsonl

parity_cases._why: Audit-3 finding #12: the design asserted the pilot uses five parity cases while the list itself had grown to seven. Generating the list from here means the count and the list cannot disagree.
parity_cases.note: Every case below is judged on ALL SEVEN points of section 5.5 - init result, [CFG] fingerprint, full order request/result trace including rejections, trade list, end-state positions/pendings, terminal side effects, errors - never on the trade list alone. All must pass before any cell's evidence counts.

rows.what it compares: wrapper vs parent, compiled defaults, XAUUSD H1
wrapper vs parent, pilot .set, XAUUSD H4
rows.what it proves: equivalence under the config the pilot actually runs

rows.what it compares: a config that provably opens trades
rows.what it proves: a run where both sides open nothing cannot be mistaken for agreement

rows.what it compares: _42_RiskPct paired with an SLMode yielding no distance, which MM-SAFETY-001 fails at OnInit
rows.what it proves: both sides refuse, for the same reason - parity can tell refused from silent

rows.what it compares: a locked parameter absent from the wrapper's Inputs page
rows.what it proves: absent from the page AND its value provably applied

rows.what it compares: a locked value changed in the registry, regenerated
rows.what it proves: behaviour changes, and parity vs the parent configured the same way still passes - lock is not ignore

rows.what it compares: delete the generated tree, regenerate from the registry
rows.what it proves: byte-identical .mq5 - NOT .ex5, MQL5 compilation is not reproducible, staleness is judged by mtime

entity.description: Discriminator. Every persisted instance carries it, including CSV-backed rows.

OwnerRef.description: The ONLY legal way for a Factory OS artifact to carry a fact owned elsewhere. Pins the owner at a commit so the reference cannot silently drift, exactly as the existing event log does. Rev 1's mutable copies are replaced by this everywhere.
OwnerRef.x-enforced-by: _triage/factory_os/run_schema_fixtures.py: AJV validates each live governed registry row, then the existing candidate.owner_ref_problems resolver checks R1 commit_oid:path, R2 blob_oid, R3 raw_sha256 and R4 anchor uniqueness. Synthetic or malformed pins refuse the governed schema/commit path.

anchor.description: must occur EXACTLY once in the blob and contain no spaces - inherited constraint from the event log utility

Hypothesis.x-enforced-by: hypothesis_validator: status transitions, and the refusal to register without a falsifier
Hypothesis.description: GENUINELY NEW only in part. Audit P0-2: the causal claim, acceptance criteria and execution context of a hypothesis already live in taskboard pre-registration. This entity therefore stores the STRUCTURED, MACHINE-READ fields (identity, architecture digest, module set, coupling) and REFERENCES the taskboard for the prose. It must not restate acceptance criteria.

architecture_digest.description: hash of (entry, exit_owner, stack_owner, lot_owner, recovery, hedge, regime). Change here MECHANICALLY forces a new revision.

experimental.description: REQUIRED, not defaulted. Audit P1: JSON Schema `default` does not populate a missing field, so a consumer would have read absent as false and let an experimental module reach a promotion path.

preregistration_ref.description: the taskboard order that owns the causal claim, falsifier and pre-registered bars. This entity does NOT copy them.

ModuleUse.x-enforced-by: candidate.py: validates the module token/stability contract before CandidatePayload identity is accepted
ModuleUse.description: A capability token plus the stability of the module behind it. Audit P1: without per-module stability, an EXPERIMENTAL module's evidence could reach a Candidate.

ParameterBinding.x-enforced-by: check_registries.py: required-field floor and registry resolver reachability; optimize_guard consumes the same resolver
ParameterBinding.description: NEW ENTITY answering the audit: rev 1 put role=LOCKED/TUNABLE on the GLOBAL parameter definition, but locked-ness is per hypothesis - the same input can be LOCKED in B14-H01 and TUNABLE in B14-H02. Marking it globally would make optimize_guard refuse it on every Boss. docs/PARAM_REGISTRY.csv keeps permanent semantics (owner/unit/context/active_when); this binds role and locked value per hypothesis revision. The wrapper generator and optimize_guard MUST read the same resolver.

parameter.description: ORDER-672: the BARE parameter name. A build tag inside this string is REFUSED -- `StackMode[LAB_ENTRY_16]` encodes two facts in the join key, which produced F1 (a tagged binding invisible to its only consumer: bare => AMBIGUOUS, tagged => unseen, jointly unsatisfiable) and half of S7 (last-wins across rows that disagree). The tag lives in build_tag. Two encodings of one fact is the defect, not a migration path.

parameter_pid.description: R4 global five-digit parameter identity; it must resolve back to parameter exactly.

build_tag.description: ORDER-672: which BUILD this binding is about, or null for "every build of the revision". A field, not a suffix -- so "these rows disagree, therefore the binding must name the tag" is representable IN THE DATA rather than inferred by whichever call site remembered to run a parser. A second parser of that string is a second resolver.

locked_value.description: required when role=LOCKED; emitted as a const by the generator

definition_ref.description: pins the docs/PARAM_REGISTRY.csv row that owns this parameter's permanent semantics

TestUniverse.description: One of the two facts the audit agreed is GENUINELY unowned: a versioned, mandatory symbol x TF set has no canonical artifact today.

broker_map.description: lane id -> broker symbol. Real cases: DE40 traded as GER40; USDJPYm/EURUSDm suffixed.

swap_mode.description: MEASURED. The tester charges POINTS-mode swap (XAUUSD verified -29.25) but not INTEREST_CURRENT (BTCUSD -14.67%/yr), which must then be deducted post-hoc from measured holding time.

InstrumentProfile.x-enforced-by: check_registries.py: required-field floor and profile content-hash/version registry checks
InstrumentProfile.description: PARTLY owned already: baseline semantics and starting values live in ea_template/OPTIMIZATION_PROCEDURE_V2.md section 4. This entity owns only the broker/lane mapping layer and pins the rest by reference. Audit P1: a mutable profile string id let profile CONTENT change under a fixed id while a Candidate still looked valid - hence content_hash + version.

content_hash.description: hash of the RESOLVED profile content. Candidates hash this, not the id.

MetricRef.x-enforced-by: run_schema_fixtures.py: ajv validates the pf/pf_state conditional in BOTH directions, over the crafted fixtures AND over every live row of every registry store
MetricRef.description: NEW. Audit P1: rev 1's CoverageCell held MAIN and BWD metrics beside ONE lane and ONE data_fingerprint - but the fingerprint includes the window, so MAIN and BWD can never share one. The pair could be filled from different lanes and rendered as if same-lane. Every metric now carries its own provenance. ORDER-1250 (owner-ratified 2026-08-03): `pf` is NULLABLE and travels with a required `pf_state`. The pilot found a cell -- USDJPY H1, 99 trades, 99 winners, gross_loss = 0 -- whose profit factor has NO DENOMINATOR. `pf` was `number`, so that cell could only be stored by writing a number that is not true: the tester prints `0` there, and ORDER-1230 already had to repair exactly that inversion, where the best win rate in the matrix rendered as the worst result in it. A bare nullable would have been enough to REPRESENT the case and not enough to make it UNFAKEABLE, so the reason rides along with the number and the two are bound in both directions: DEFINED demands a number, UNDEFINED_NO_LOSSES demands null. A cell with zero trades also has no denominator and is UNDEFINED_NO_LOSSES -- literally true, and `trades` is required beside it so a reader can tell the two apart.

pf.description: null ONLY with pf_state = UNDEFINED_NO_LOSSES. Never 0 to mean undefined: 0 is a real PF (a run with winners worth nothing) and the tester prints it for both, which is how the inversion happened.

pf_state.description: Why pf is or is not a number. Required so that an absent denominator has to be DECLARED rather than encoded as a value.

CoverageCell.x-writer: automation for state; claude only for not_applicable_reason
CoverageCell.x-enforced-by: coverage_validator: comparison-group same-lane rule; MASTER_BACKLOG section 2 regenerated from this, never hand-edited
CoverageCell.description: Audit P0-2: MASTER_BACKLOG.md declares itself owner of the coverage matrix. This entity does NOT replace it - MASTER_BACKLOG section 2 becomes GENERATED from these rows, and the ownership move is recorded in the migration table. Metrics are MetricRefs, never bare numbers.

metrics.description: PF is unrepresentable without trades and dd_pct by construction: two BWD-clearing hosts had 52 and 62 trades at under 2% DD while every failing host had 343-473.

boundary_hit.description: true = best result on a grid edge; the cell may NOT be closed until the range is expanded

ExecutionKey.x-enforced-by: scheduler.py: canonical execution-key digest and cache/queue identity gate
ExecutionKey.description: The complete new simulator input identity. Currency is frozen to the USD runner contract; account_unit and the resolved terminal FileVersion build are distinct cache dimensions. effective_config_hash remains the existing chart/set/config/surface fingerprint, not account or terminal identity. ini_sha256 remains attempt forensics because it does not exist before launch.

leverage.description: written as 1:N in the ini and asserted post-run; a bare Leverage=N is a silent no-op

terminal_build.description: numeric build component mechanically read from the resolved terminal64.exe FileVersion; never inferred from lane or caller text

LegacyExecutionKey.description: Closed historical unit/build-unknown shape. It is readable for audit only and cannot equal a new ExecutionKey. The optional ini_hash is the exact pre-2026-08-02 persisted form and is removed only for the established legacy digest migration.

RunAttempt.x-enforced-by: scheduler.py: append-only transition validator and durable per-attempt surface/ini forensics
RunAttempt.description: One append-only record. Audit P1: rev 1 had ONE attempt field and ONE state on the manifest while the design claimed every attempt was kept, and it was not crash-safe. Transitions are now appended, never overwritten.

lease.description: SELF-REVIEW FIX: rev 3 required `pid` on the lease, but LEASED happens BEFORE any process exists - the lane is reserved first. A schema that demands a fact nobody can know yet is a schema that gets filled with a placeholder. pid moves to process_observed and is not part of the lease.

expires_at.description: without an expiry a machine that died holding a lease keeps the lane forever

launch_intent_at.description: written BEFORE spawn. Its presence with no process_observed means the crash happened around the spawn and the resume must RECONCILE (is an MT5 already running on this lane?) rather than launch again.

report_path.description: the report path bound by LAUNCH_INTENT for this attempt; later transitions cannot replace that identity

process_observed.description: SELF-REVIEW FIX: rev 3 had a single `launched_at` written before launch, which cannot distinguish crash-before-spawn from crash-after-spawn - the exact hole the field was added to close. Two records, so the pair is decidable.

ini_sha256.description: USER DECISION 2026-08-02 (USER_DECISIONS_PENDING item 6): the sha256 of the .ini the runner actually wrote, recorded PER ATTEMPT and AFTER the file exists. It moved here from ExecutionKey, where it was a fact nobody could know at the moment the key was needed. Identity lives in the key; forensics - what exactly was handed to the tester - lives here, where it can be true.

set_surface_state.description: ORDER-1290. The exact Get-SetSurfaceState result made durable: the committed .set path and bytes, the Inputs.mqh source bytes and build surface, and the ExecutionKey/run binding. FULL is reproducible; UNDECLARED/MISMATCH/UNREADABLE/NOSETFILE is not accepted as complete evidence.

exit_code.description: persisted immediately on receipt - the freshness guard needs exit 0/3 and cannot reconstruct it

failure_class.description: decision 18 permits a re-run of an identical ExecutionKey only after an execution or a tester error. USER DECISION 2026-08-02 (USER_DECISIONS_PENDING item 7) ratified that those are two CATEGORIES, not two enum members: tester = TESTER_ERROR; execution = TERMINAL_ERROR, TIMEOUT, KILLED, LEASE_LOST; neither, and therefore still blocked = CONFIG_REJECTED. This description used to name only TESTER_ERROR and TERMINAL_ERROR, and read literally it made a machine crash a permanent block on the configuration - in the slice whose whole purpose is recovery.

event_id.description: id returned by the existing event-log append, so a crash between append and EVIDENCE_REGISTERED does not duplicate the occurrence on retry

RunTransition.x-owner-file: factory/runs/<run_id>.jsonl - ONE OF THESE PER LINE, append-only
RunTransition.x-enforced-by: scheduler: reconcile process + report + event store BEFORE any retry; monotonic transition validator
RunTransition.description: SELF-REVIEW FIX (2026-07-30): rev 3 stored a `RunJournal` OBJECT containing an attempts ARRAY at a path described as one-transition-per-line append-only. Those cannot both be true - appending a transition to an in-object array means rewriting the whole object, which is not append-only, so the crash-safety claim was unsupported by its own storage contract. The PERSISTED entity is this: one transition, one line. `RunJournal` is now a derived read-model that is never written.

execution_key.description: written once, on the QUEUED line

RunTransition.x-enforced-by: _triage/factory_os/run_schema_fixtures.py: ajv validates every committed factory/runs/*.jsonl RunTransition row; exactly three byte-pinned historical manifests are visible LEGACY_EXCEPTION results until their event-log occurrence is durable

RunJournal.x-enforced-by: scheduler.py: folds and validates the RunTransition lines into the derived journal read-model
RunJournal.x-owner-file: NONE - derived by folding the RunTransition lines of one run_id. Never persisted, never written.
RunJournal.description: Read-model only. Realizes EVOLUTION_PLAN section 20.8 Contract B. Occurrence metadata and hashes only - the experiment event log remains the owner of the experiment timeline; this fold owns ONLY scheduler recovery state, which the audit agreed is a genuinely new fact.

EvidenceRef.description: Audit P0-2: rev 1 proposed factory/evidence/index.csv, duplicating an evidence manifest that already exists with its own schema (evidence-v1.schema.json). The Factory OS registers through the EXISTING utility and adds nothing. Known inherited constraints: .ex5 binaries are gitignored and need git add -f; the path pattern forbids parentheses and spaces; tick history uses a committed provenance descriptor.

CandidatePayload.x-enforced-by: candidate.py: canonical payload digest, full input surface, module stability, profile hashes, and cited-run linkage
CandidatePayload.description: THE HASHED OBJECT. Audit P1: rev 1 made candidate_id a required member of the object whose hash it was defined to be - id = hash(manifest containing id) has no normal construction, so a team would have hashed a different payload than the validator and quietly disabled the check. The id is now the hash of THIS object, which does not contain it. Also widened per the audit: module set with stability, resolved profile CONTENT hashes, generator/allowlist/source hashes, effective config, and evidence as a list with per-window provenance rather than one lane.

experimental.description: MUST be false for any candidate on a promotion path; the validator additionally resolves every evidence -> run -> module set and fails if any module is not CERTIFIABLE

build_tag.description: ORDER-1268. The build whose input surface `parameters` claims to BE. Added because `parameters` was required to be the FULL effective surface while nothing named the surface it was full OF, so the only enforceable reading of the rule was non-emptiness - and a one-key map validated clean. Inputs.mqh declares StackMode eight times, once per LAB_ENTRY tag, and no single build exposes all 184 declarations, so a parameter map without its build is a map against no surface at all.

parameters.description: FULL effective surface OF build_tag, key for key. A partial set lets unlisted inputs be filled from the per-terminal tester cache - the documented root cause of the ORDER-165 8/8 false drift. ORDER-1268: enforced by resolving build_tag's surface out of ea_template/core/Inputs.mqh and comparing key sets, through the same setfile.surface_problems the .set reader uses - one policy, two callers.

profiles.description: content hashes, not mutable string ids - otherwise instrument_profiles could change under a fixed id and the candidate would still look valid

evidence.description: per window, each with its own run/lane/fingerprint - MAIN and BWD cannot share a fingerprint and must not be flattened to one

CandidateManifest.x-enforced-by: candidate_validator: MUST recompute sha256 over the canonical serialization of `payload` and compare to candidate_digest. The schema checks the PATTERN only - it cannot verify a hash.

candidate_id.description: DISPLAY id = first 12 hex of candidate_digest. Never the hash input.

candidate_digest.description: full sha256 over the canonical serialization of `payload` - which does not contain it

scorecard_ref.description: the verdict TEXT lives in EA_SCORECARD_AND_REGISTRY.md and is never copied here

MagicAllocation.x-writer: automation allocates; claude approves; user ratifies scope changes
MagicAllocation.x-enforced-by: allocator: global uniqueness for NEW allocations; check_state.ps1 remains the account|magic backstop
MagicAllocation.x-legacy-exception-set-note: ORDER-1260 #4: THE closed set, in the one place that is both machine-readable and already carries the user decision below. magic.declared_legacy_magics() reads it and store_problems M7 compares the store against it. Before this, membership was bound only to 'one allocated_at_commit' (M6) - and a fourth legacy row that copied the cutover oid out of the file it was attacking passed validate_allocation, store_problems and inventory_problems against the real 60-row store. Adding a member here is a USER DECISION about holding account-scoped uniqueness open forever; it is deliberately not a code change, and it is deliberately not a fourth prose copy
MagicAllocation.description: USER DECISION 2026-07-30: uniqueness scope moves to GLOBAL, per Grill decision 56. This CONTRADICTS the account|magic invariant currently in PROJECT_STATE.md section 3, so that invariant must be amended by the user in the Decision log before this is built. The audit is correct that the current fleet violates global uniqueness: magics 990103, 991001 and 991002 each appear on two accounts, and 991001 is on real money. Those are recorded as legacy_exception and FROZEN until their judge date - the live fleet is never renumbered as a side effect of adopting this scope. Renumbering, if ever done, is a separate user-approved order.

scope.description: GLOBAL for everything allocated from now on; LEGACY_ACCOUNT_SCOPED only for the pre-existing collisions

legacy_accounts.description: populated only for legacy exceptions; frozen until judge

allocated_to.description: candidate_id. Deployment status is NOT copied here - DEPLOYMENTS.csv owns it.

status.description: RETIRED is never re-issued - a reused magic silently re-attributes historical deals

imported_in_cutover.description: RE-AUDIT P1: legacy exceptions are a CLOSED SET imported once, not an open category. Rev 2 let an unlimited number of new LEGACY_ACCOUNT_SCOPED rows be minted, which would have quietly reintroduced account-scoped magics forever. The allocator refuses a legacy row with imported_in_cutover=false after the cutover commit.

then.description: scope and the exception flags must agree, and a legacy exception exists precisely because the magic is on more than one account

DeploymentAttestationEvent.x-enforced-by: attestation_validator: no actor other than user/claude may append an event that changes candidate_id or status; automation may append OBSERVED events only
DeploymentAttestationEvent.description: Audit P1: rev 1 had a mutable DeploymentAttestation whose candidate_id, state and core revision could be overwritten, so automation could have advanced a deployment to a new revision without the user ever moving the champion. Deployment STATE stays in DEPLOYMENTS.csv; this is an append-only attestation history.

prev_hash.description: ORDER-1260 #3: sha256 of the canonical bytes of the PREVIOUS line, or 64 zeros for the first. Replay alone could not tell an appended log from an edited one - an edited event is still a well-formed event in a well-ordered log - so attestation.validate_event A8 chains them. It protects every event that has a successor; the LAST line is only protected by pinning the head elsewhere

authorization_ref.description: REQUIRED for any event that is not OBSERVED - the human decision that authorized it

WorkReceipt.x-enforced-by: receipt_validator: only the user may write CANCELLED_BY_USER
WorkReceipt.description: Audit P1 (governance): rev 1 declared the writer as 'any agent', but AGENTS.md section 2 permits an agent to write only its own taskboard order row plus new reports/CSV/sets per order. Opening a new writer surface REQUIRES the user to ratify an AGENTS.md permission-table change FIRST. Audit P0-2 also applies: for work that already has an ORDER, title/status/owner/acceptance are the taskboard's - this entity references them. A Receipt is genuinely new ONLY for a chat commitment that is not yet an Order.

order_ref.description: when present, the taskboard owns status/acceptance/owner and this Receipt must NOT restate them

status.description: DONE is deliberately absent - DONE is not closed. No AGING/NEGLECTED state exists either.

then.description: RE-AUDIT P0: a Receipt that references an ORDER may NOT also carry title/owner/status/acceptance. Those are taskboard facts, and holding a second mutable copy is the ownership fork this design exists to prevent - Order REVIEWED while Receipt still IN_PROGRESS. Read them through order_ref.

else.description: a Receipt with no Order is the only case where it owns these - a chat commitment not yet formalised

then.description: Audit P1: rev 1 used anyOf here, so one of the two sufficed - which produced exactly the indefinitely-parked item the design says it prevents. Both are now required.

SystemFinding.x-enforced-by: finding_validator: RUNTIME resolves only after two consecutive healthy checks; GOVERNANCE/AUDIT/DEPLOYMENT_DRIFT never auto-close
SystemFinding.description: New ONLY for the stable lifecycle and identity. The detector state itself is owned by the snapshot; this references it.

finding_id.description: INTERNAL ONLY. Its stable key may legitimately contain an account number, a magic, or a strategy name (e.g. FND-sensor-159503454), so it MUST NOT be serialized into any online or Telegram surface.

public_id.description: RE-AUDIT P1: opaque projection-safe identifier - the ONLY finding id a SafeProjection may carry. Rev 2 leaked the raw finding_id into the online projection while carefully masking account numbers two fields away.

detector_ref.description: RE-AUDIT P0: the snapshot owns detector state. Without a pinned reference this entity becomes a second, drifting copy - snapshot RESOLVED while the finding still reads OPEN.

severity.description: part of the alert dedupe key - audit P1: dedupe on (id,state) alone would swallow a warning that escalated to real-money critical while the state stayed OPEN

material_revision.description: REQUIRED. Bumped whenever the payload materially changes, and part of the dedupe key alongside severity - dedupe on (id,state) alone swallows a WARN that escalates to REAL_MONEY while the state stays OPEN

IdeaRef.description: Audit P0-2: rev 1 proposed ops/ideas.csv, but INTAKE_QUEUE.md opens by declaring itself the single place for every new source and strategy drop. There is no second intake. What is genuinely missing is a STABLE ID and exact-URL dedupe, so those are added AS COLUMNS TO THE EXISTING OWNER and this entity is only the machine-readable projection of a row.

ControlRoomSnapshotV5.x-enforced-by: snapshot_validator: reconciliation_clear is COMPUTED and MUST NOT be read from input
ControlRoomSnapshotV5.description: RE-AUDIT P0 FIX: rev 2 declared `SnapshotMeta` to be the schema of control_room_snapshot.json, but it described a FLAT root {entity, schema, version, ...} while the real persisted document is {meta:{...}, system_health:[...], deployments, judge_readiness, judge_cohorts, attestation, unknown_magics, floating_risk, summary} - nine top-level keys. A validator built to that schema would have validated a shape that never exists and reported the pipeline schema-clean while never touching the actual snapshot. This entity is the WHOLE document; SnapshotMeta is now the schema of its `meta` property only. ORDER-601 part 2: this root is now CLOSED. It was `additionalProperties: true` on the argument that the file versions additively, but the two facts do not imply each other - additive versioning means no field is REMOVED or RENAMED between versions, and it is satisfied by declaring each new domain here. An open root means a whole top-level domain can appear that no contract describes and no reader is required to handle, which is the same shape as the source array that silently dropped a missing file. The eleven keys below cover every top-level key the real v4 document has; closing the root therefore costs nothing today and forces the next domain to be declared. Adding a domain is a one-line edit HERE, which is the point: it becomes a reviewable act instead of a side effect.

judge_cohorts.description: MEASURED 2026-07-31 (ORDER-612 / S4): this was `type: object` and the real document has always carried an ARRAY of 17 per-judge-date cohort rollups (scripts/control_room_snapshot.ps1 `$cohorts`). The first build of a v5 document was refused by ajv naming `/judge_cohorts`, which is how it was found. It is the same defect class as rev 2's flat root: a contract that claims to describe a file and describes a shape the file never has. Nothing caught it earlier because no fixture ever validated the REAL document -- which is exactly what C1 of this order requires and why C1 is worded as a flip of that line rather than as a claim about it.

ReconciliationEvidence.x-owner-file: the `meta.reconciliation` property of a SnapshotBuilderInput and of portfolio/control_room_snapshot.json
ReconciliationEvidence.x-enforced-by: snapshot_validator: this object is the INPUT to the reconciliation_clear computation and never contains the answer
ReconciliationEvidence.description: ORDER-601 / audit-5 Q2. `reconciliation_clear` used to live here, which made the contract unsatisfiable: it was REQUIRED in the persisted document and a writer-supplied value had to be REJECTED, and no validator inspecting one document can tell 'computed' from 'typed'. The evidence and the verdict are now different objects. Because this object is CLOSED and has no `reconciliation_clear` property, a builder that supplies one is refused by the schema itself - no special-case code, and the rejection names the property. Audit-5 also found every nested integer here lacked `minimum: 0`, so `actionable:-1, running:1` balanced every equation and validated; the bounds below close that.

categories.description: the equation's right-hand side must be ENCODED, not implied in prose

SnapshotVerdict.x-owner-file: the `verdict` property of portfolio/control_room_snapshot.json - written ONLY by snapshot_validator
SnapshotVerdict.x-enforced-by: snapshot_validator.verify_snapshot: recomputes reconciliation_clear from the persisted evidence and refuses a document whose stored verdict does not match. Proves INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, not authenticity: read_ok/age_hours/path/sha256/mtime and the reconciliation counts are builder claims taken at face value (Codex audit 6 accepted a document whose sources all pointed at a nonexistent drive with mtime 2099). Deriving them from the real files and re-hashing on read is S4. NOT on every READ - Codex audit 6 measured that no reader calls load_verified(); wiring readers is S4, so the honest status today is BUILT_NOT_WIRED
SnapshotVerdict.description: ORDER-601. JSON Schema can prove this boolean is well-typed; it cannot prove who wrote it. Audit-5's surviving attack was a hand-authored output with sources=[] and reconciliation_clear=true, which is structurally valid. The defence is not the schema, it is that every reader must obtain the document through the verifier that recomputes this from `meta.reconciliation` and the source list. `reasons` is a CLOSED enum so a false verdict cannot be explained in free text nobody parses.

reconciliation_clear.description: COMPUTED, never supplied. True only when every mandatory source is present, read_ok and fresh; discovered==categorized; the category sum matches; the coverage sum matches; duplicates==0; conflicts==0; unclassified==0; and categories.actionable==0. SCOPE - narrower than the old name promised: computed from meta.reconciliation and the source rows ONLY. It was called `all_clear` until Codex audit 6 built a document with a NO_SENSOR fleet sensor, a BLIND floating-risk sensor, missing kill/judge controls, an UNCLASSIFIED unknown magic and missing attestation, and it verified true - because none of those domains reach the computation. system_health, floating_risk, deployments.gaps, unknown_magics, attestation, judge_readiness and summary are carried through UNCHECKED. Do not render this as Control Room health.

reasons.description: empty if and only if reconciliation_clear is true - the two must not be able to disagree

code.description: MISSING and UNREADABLE are separate codes on purpose: 'cannot read it' and 'it is not there' have opposite fixes and this repo has collapsed them before

detail.description: the source name, or the two numbers that failed to match - so a fixture can assert WHICH instance fired

SnapshotBuilderInput.x-owner-file: NONE - transient. Produced by the snapshot builder, consumed by snapshot_validator, never persisted.
SnapshotBuilderInput.x-enforced-by: snapshot_validator.build_snapshot: refuses a supplied answer via a recursive forbidden-key scan (verdict / reconciliation_clear / all_clear / reasons) UNCONDITIONALLY; refuses a schema-invalid input only when called with ajv_schema_validator, which the fast computation suite does not do. Treat the schema half as enforced at the load_verified() boundary, not on every code path
SnapshotBuilderInput.description: ORDER-601 / audit-5 Q2: the builder side of the boundary. It carries the same facts as the persisted document but has NO `verdict` property and, because it is closed, cannot acquire one. That is what makes 'reconciliation_clear is computed, never supplied' checkable by the schema instead of by a code path somebody can special-case.

judge_cohorts.description: MEASURED 2026-07-31 (ORDER-612 / S4): this was `type: object` and the real document has always carried an ARRAY of 17 per-judge-date cohort rollups (scripts/control_room_snapshot.ps1 `$cohorts`). The first build of a v5 document was refused by ajv naming `/judge_cohorts`, which is how it was found. It is the same defect class as rev 2's flat root: a contract that claims to describe a file and describes a shape the file never has. Nothing caught it earlier because no fixture ever validated the REAL document -- which is exactly what C1 of this order requires and why C1 is worded as a flip of that line rather than as a claim about it.

RuntimeIdentityObserved.description: Runtime identity emitted by the EA. Validation state is added by the collection boundary, not supplied by the EA. Collected sidecars are persisted evidence/storage locations, and no single canonical owner currently owns the observation corpus.
RuntimeIdentityObserved.x-enforced-by: runtime_identity.py: validates the EA-emitted identity shape and build/artifact evidence

RuntimeIdentityRecord.description: Observed runtime identity plus canonical validator outcome.
RuntimeIdentityRecord.x-enforced-by: runtime_identity.py: annotates collected identity records with fail-closed validation state

RuntimeIdentitySummary.x-enforced-by: monitor_coverage.ps1: red-lines missing, legacy, mixed, or failed runtime identity evidence

SnapshotMeta.x-enforced-by: snapshot_validator.py: parent ControlRoomSnapshot validation recomputes mandatory-source reconciliation and freshness
SnapshotMeta.description: The META SUB-OBJECT ONLY - not the whole file. Audit P1 (rev 1): reconciliation_clear was a writer-supplied boolean, `fresh` was not required, there was no mandatory-source registry and no category totals, so a snapshot with a missing mandatory source - or one that simply omitted the source from the array - could report reconciliation_clear:true and satisfy the equation with 0=0. Version note: HEAD is already v4; the Factory domain lands as v5.

version.description: v5+ for anything carrying the Factory domain; v4 already exists at HEAD

mandatory_sources.description: the REGISTRY of what must be present, kept separate from what was discovered - otherwise a missing source is indistinguishable from one that was never expected. `uniqueItems` because a registry naming the same source twice makes its own cardinality unreadable; a DUPLICATE name in the `sources` array below is not expressible in JSON Schema and is snapshot_validator's DUPLICATE_SOURCE_NAME predicate instead.

read_ok.description: false must stay distinguishable from 'read fine, found nothing' in EVERY consumer

fresh.description: DERIVED, and the validator does not trust the supplied value: it recomputes fresh from `age_hours` against `stale_bar_hours` and overwrites this on the way out. Present because the real v4 consumers read it. A caller-supplied `fresh: true` on an over-the-bar row therefore does NOT buy an reconciliation_clear - there is a fixture for exactly that.

path.description: COMPATIBILITY: the real v4 source rows are {path, sha256, mtime, age_hours} (scripts/control_room_snapshot.ps1 FileMeta) and carry no `name` at all. These three were absent from this closed row, so a builder holding the real metadata could not even be expressed at the boundary, let alone preserve it. Reconciling `path` with `name` as the identity is S4's job; carrying it through is this order's.

stale_bar_hours.description: COMPATIBILITY: exists in the real v4 file (scripts/control_room_snapshot.ps1). The validator derives freshness from this, never from a hardcoded threshold and never from a caller-supplied `fresh`.

decision_bar_trades.description: COMPATIBILITY: exists in the real v4 file. Audit 3 found the schema silently dropped it.

counting_method.description: COMPATIBILITY: exists in the real v4 file. Audit 3 found the schema silently dropped it.

runtime_identity_required.description: Current VPS DEMO/forward-test snapshots require runtime identity; legacy snapshots may omit this policy flag.

SafeProjection.x-enforced-by: projection_validator: recursive forbidden-key scan + synthetic secret/account fixtures; the Telegram sender MUST NOT be able to read the full snapshot
SafeProjection.description: NEW, answering the audit: the design claimed the online projection was 'safe by construction' but no construction existed, while the real snapshot carries account IDs, balance, equity, floating P/L and exact open lots. This is an allowlist-only derived DTO. Anything not listed here cannot reach an online or Telegram surface.

build_id.description: ORDER-1267 Part 2: constrained because it was an unconstrained string that the notifier interpolates verbatim into the text it sends. Shape DERIVED, not invented -- snapshot_build.compute_build_id returns sha256(...).hexdigest()[:16].

generated_at.description: ORDER-1267 Part 2, same reasoning and same route as build_id. Shape DERIVED -- control_room_snapshot.ps1 writes $now.ToString('s'): yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss, no fraction, no zone.

items.description: no account number, no balance, no equity, no P/L amount, no lot size, no strategy identifier

sensor_state.description: CONFLICT (ORDER-1267 #2, owner-ratified 2026-08-04) is what the two detectors DISAGREEING renders - control_center.sensors_disagree() owns the rule and safe_projection.build() calls it. It is not a state any detector emits, so it is absent from SENSOR_STATE_MAP's keys and present in its target vocabulary

dd_pct_band.description: a BAND, not a number - a percentage plus a known base equity reconstructs the money amount

items.description: public_id ONLY. The internal finding_id may embed an account, a magic or a strategy name and must never reach this surface.

AlertEvent.x-owner-file: (in memory only) an AlertEvent is never persisted; ops/delivery_ledger.jsonl records that one existed
AlertEvent.x-enforced-by: notifier.assert_sendable: the declared SHAPE checked against this file, PLUS safe_projection.scan_forbidden run with the real snapshot secret list - the layer the sender structurally cannot run
AlertEvent.description: NEW in S12. The ONLY thing that crosses the seam from the local side to a channel. Allowlist-only and closed, because `text` is free-form and is therefore the one field on which a careless renderer can write an account number onto the wire. Everything else here is an enum or a hashed id.

channel.description: design 7.3 names two bots on ONE event system. The channel is decided by the severity routing table the owner ratified on 2026-08-02, not by a chat id in a config file.

public_id.description: The internal finding_id may embed an account, a magic or an EA name and MUST NOT travel. This is safe_projection.public_id() of it, so the id on Telegram and the id on the dashboard are pinned together as design 7.3 requires.

class.description: Safe to send: a four-value closed enum with no identity in it. It is what makes a thin alert actionable at 3am without a detail line.

material_revision.description: Part of the dedupe key. It cannot be computed from the SafeProjection - that surface carries public_id/severity/state and nothing else - so it is produced local-side by notifier.observe() from ops/finding_journal.jsonl. Naming that gap is the point.

dedupe_key.description: public_id + state + severity + material_revision, per design 7.3. Rev 1 deduped on (id, state), which suppressed a WARN escalating to REAL_MONEY while the state stayed OPEN.

text.description: The rendered message. The ONLY free-form field, and therefore the one assert_sendable's literal scan exists for.

AlertDelivery.x-enforced-by: notifier.deliver: every event produces exactly one line whatever happened, and dedupe reads DELIVERED and nothing else
AlertDelivery.description: NEW in S12. One line per attempted delivery. Without it, dedupe is a claim about SENDING rather than about ARRIVING, and a replay after an outage re-alerts what already landed. Carries a channel NAME and never a chat id: a chat id is a delivery credential.

outcome.description: UNCONFIGURED and FAILED are STATED failures that make the CLI exit non-zero. A sender that cannot send and reports nothing is indistinguishable from a quiet fleet. UNCONFIGURED_REGRESSION (ORDER-1261 #6) is the third: a channel that HAS delivered before and now has no credential. It is split from UNCONFIGURED because that one routes to exit 4, which ORDER-219 deliberately mutes in the daily chain - correct for 'the owner has not made the bot yet', wrong for 'the credential that was working is gone'

receipt.description: The provider's message id, which is what makes 'did this arrive' answerable. Null for every outcome that is not DELIVERED.

openclaw.description: design 10 requires alerts to work with OpenClaw stopped. Recording the OBSERVED gateway state beside the receipt turns that from a claim in a handoff into a measurement stored next to the evidence. UNKNOWN is a real third answer and is never collapsed onto NOT_RUNNING.

transport_kind.description: Optional for legacy ledger rows; newly emitted rows carry the runtime transport classification. UNKNOWN is conservative and does not prove a credentialed transport.

ExperimentContract.x-enforced-by: _triage/factory_os/qi_1.py: strict shape, OwnerRef, R4 strategy/PID resolution, and append-only writes
ExperimentContract.description: Immutable QI-1 preregistration. It stores expected implementation identity; observed run identity is joined by the validator.

ExperimentResult.x-enforced-by: _triage/factory_os/qi_1.py: strict shape, run/evidence identity binding, and append-only writes
ExperimentResult.description: Immutable QI-1 result pointer. It carries no normalized metrics; evidence remains the metric authority.
